ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (as amended) — national AML/CFT framework and customer due diligence; Decreto de Gabinete No. 344 de 17 de septiembre de 2021 — creation and governance of the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (RBF); Resolución No. 201-6337 de 24 de junio de 2021 (Dirección General de Ingresos / MEF) — RBF registration and beneficial ownership parameters; Ley 70 de 30 de enero de 2019 and associated CRS/FATCA AEOI regulations — automatic exchange of information; Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) Resolución No. 036-2021 — mandatory CDD, EDD, and Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) rules; Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 — Private Interest Foundation (PIF) enabling statute and public registry filing requirements.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notario Público de la República de Panamá (Panamanian Public Notary)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization (no apostille required); submitted in original to the Registro Público de Panamá for inscription by the resident agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of the Founder (fundador) and each initial member of the Foundation Council

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization) plus certified Spanish translation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 1995 (Private Interest Foundation Law), as amended by Ley No. 2 de 2014; Articles 1-32; Complementary provisions of the Código Judicial (Non-Contentious Jurisdiction) and Public Registry tariff rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución / Acta de Fundación (Public Deed of Formation of Private Interest Foundation), submitted via Notary and registered at the Public Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum initial endowment of USD 10,000 (or equivalent in any currency) declared in the Foundation Charter; no government escrow account is required and the endowment may represent future assets or be contributed within the first fiscal year.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF [PA_PIF FOUNDATION], adopted at the registered office in Panama City. FIRST: The Council accepts the initial endowment of USD 10,000 constituting the Foundation's patrimony. SECOND: The registered office is adopted at [Address], Panama City, Republic of Panama. THIRD: The Council appoints [Name] as President, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Treasurer to administer the Foundation. FOURTH: The President is authorized to execute banking powers, sign supplier agreements, and effect filings with the Public Registry and DGI. FIFTH: The Internal Regulations are adopted. The Secretary shall retain the minute files.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search, Charter Drafting, and Notarial Execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (online name availability); Notaría Pública in Panama City
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an online availability search for the proposed foundation name; if available, procure formal name clearance. Instruct a Panamanian notary to prepare and execute the Foundation Charter (Escritura Pública de Constitución) including: foundation denomination, registered office, initial endowment of USD 10,000, purpose (manufacture of digital X-ray flat panel detectors), Foundation Council members, founder's reserved powers, beneficiary provisions, and amendment/dissolution rules. The founder signs before the notary; if the founder is non-resident, execute a power of attorney authenticated by the corresponding consulate or Apostille.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of passport of Founder
Power of attorney to Panamanian law firm (if founder absent)
Name availability/clearance report from Public Registry
Declaration of initial endowment and source of funds
Copy of Foundation Council members' passports and backgrounds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit up to 3 alternative names; if the notary raises observations on endowment or purpose clauses, restate the charter and re-execute before the same notary at additional notarial fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (via Sistema de Inscripción en Línea)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Foundation Charter together with the insertion sheets and protocol testimony through the Registry's online inscription platform. Pay stamp duty (papel sellado) and the registry fee calculated on the declared endowment (minimum USD 10,000). Upon exam, the Registry issues the 'Inscripción de la Fundación' certificate, which evidences the legal personality of the PIF.
required_dossiers: Notarized Foundation Charter (original protocol copy)
Protocol excerpt testimony issued by the Notary
Evidence of payment of stamp duty (papel sellado)
Registry insertion fee deposit receipt
Power of attorney of the registering agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues an observation ('reparo'), respond within 30 business days supplying corrected pages and rake-off payment; if the inscription is suspended, file a formal 'reforma' amendment to align clauses and pay revival fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Identification Number (RUC) and Digital Signature Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — Sede Electrónica / Registro de Contribuyentes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, apply online for the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) and optional Firma Digital certificate. The RUC is required for banking, import/export of manufacturing equipment, invoicing, and annual tax returns (territorial taxation regime). Register the foundation's economic activity under ISIC 3250 with DGI.
required_dossiers: Registry inscription certificate of the PIF
Certified copy of the Foundation Charter
Power of attorney of the tax agent
Valid passports of the Foundation Council officers
Lease or ownership deed evidencing the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI rejects or queries the RUC application, amend the filing by submitting corrected officer data or proof of registered office; engage a tax agent to reconcile discrepancies within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating Notice (Aviso de Operación) and Zoning Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá — Dirección General de Finanzas (Vía Céntrica Window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the official Aviso de Operación form for the manufacturing plant located in the industrial/commercial zoning zone. Attach the lease title, municipal zoning certificate, registry inscription, and RUC. The Municipality issues the annual operating card enabling lawful industrial activity within the district.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate
Public Registry inscription certificate
Lease agreement or propiedad title
Municipal zoning and land-use certificate
Fire safety certificate of the premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality objects to the zoning of the premises, apply for a classification change or a conditional industrial-use permit; provide architectural plans and environmental registration to support the application and re-submit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sanitary Manufacturing License and Product Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) — Dirección de Dispositivos Médicos
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prior to commencing production, file the application for the 'Permiso Sanitario de Funcionamiento' of the medical-device manufacturing plant and the product registration dossier for digital X-ray flat panel detectors. Submit the ISO 13485 quality manual, cleanroom layout, electrical/radiation safety data, and environmental approval. MINSA schedules an on-site inspection before issuance.
required_dossiers: Foundation registration certificate
RUC certificate
Detailed product list (digital X-ray flat panel detectors, Class IIa/IIb)
ISO 13485 quality management system manual
Facility lay-out plan of vapor deposition/cleanroom areas
Environmental impact registration approval
Fire safety certificate from Bomberos
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MINSA denies or conditionally approves the license, respond to technical observations within 30 days, correct non-conformities, and request re-inspection; engage a certified medical-device consultant to facilitate re-application.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) — Dirección de Dispositivos Médicos y Dirección Nacional de Regulación Sanitaria
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permiso Sanitario de Operación para Fabricación de Dispositivos Médicos (Registro Sanitario de Dispositivos Médicos Clase IIa/IIb)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría II — Registro Ambiental (under Decreto Ejecutivo No. 123 de 2009, as amended); elevated to Categoría III (full Estudio de Impacto Ambiental) only if silane or cesium iodide inventory exceeds regulatory threshold of 20 MT annual.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater per Decreto Ejecutivo No. 54 de 2011: pH 6.0-9.0, total suspended solids ≤ 100 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 50 mg/L, COD ≤ 200 mg/L, oil and grease ≤ 20 mg/L. Air/VOC: silane and solvent vapor capture efficiency ≥ 95%, total VOC concentration ≤ 150 mg/m³ in discharged air. Solid and hazardous waste: comply with Resolución MiAMBIENTE No. 652 de 2016 requiring waste manifests and authorized disposal routes; spent cesium iodide and amorphous silicon residues are classified as hazardous, non-radioactive; waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE) managed under Ley No. 40 de 2018.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá — annual Certificado de Seguridad y Prevención de Incendios with required suppression systems for chemical/cleanroom areas; structural load inspection certificate issued by a licensed Panamanian engineer for installation of deposition chambers and detector assembly lines; occupational hazard prevention clearance from MINSA and Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) confirming workplace ergonomic and electrical safety compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Autoridad Nacional de Ingresos Públicos (ANIP) — Republic of Panama, succeeding the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, with customs and internal revenue functions consolidated under Ley No. 365 de 2023. Official digital portal: Sede Electrónica ANIP at https://www.anip.gob.pa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned Private Interest Foundation (PIF): (1) Appoint a Panama-licensed registered agent and a tax-resident fiscal representative. (2) Register the foundation charter with the Registro Público de Panamá, Section of Private Interest Foundations, obtaining the foundation registration certificate and cargo (officer) appointments. (3) File the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) application through the ANIP Sede Electrónica portal, submitting the certified and apostilled foundation deed, valid identification of the foundation's beneficiaries or council, registered agent acceptance, and fiscal representative power of attorney. (4) Request simultaneous activation of the ITBMS (VAT) registration and designation as an exporter in the national customs exporter registry (VUPE). (5) Enroll as an electronic invoicing issuer with an ANIP-authorised e-invoicing operator. (6) Complete the foundation's mandatory annual flat tax payment of USD 400 through the ANIP system. Processing normally takes 10 to 20 business days after receipt of complete documentation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope — The Panama PIF (Ley No. 25 de 1995) is a distinct legal person with segregated patrimony. Under Panama's territorial taxation model, income arising from Panamanian-source business activity is taxed at entity level under the Código Fiscal, while foreign-source income and offshore-held foundation assets remain outside the Panamanian tax net. A passive PIF that does not undertake commercial operations is liable only to the fixed USD 400 annual state fee. The foundation is not eligible for automatic pass-through or fiscal transparency treatment in Panama for income tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide a US-style check-the-box election. Available legal elections are governed by the Código Fiscal, Ley No. 25 de 1995, and ANIP administrative resolutions: (i) the foundation may, by charter amendment, elect to register as a commercial operator with the Registro Público and assume full income tax and ITBMS obligations for its Panama-source business profits; (ii) election to file as an exporter and apply zero-rated ITBMS treatment for qualifying export sales; (iii) election to maintain a passive patrimonial status while holding shares of an operating company; (iv) election to apply the special drawback or refund mechanism for VAT embedded in export production inputs; and (v) no hybrid-mismatch or check-the-box election exists under Panamanian law, so the PIF's classification is determined by its charter and registry status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios), Panama's value-added tax on transfers of movable goods and the rendering of services, enacted by Ley No. 28 de 1995 and regulated by the Código Fiscal and ANIP administrative resolutions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.36,000 (USD 36,000) of cumulative annual onerous transfers of goods and services, expressed in Panamanian balboas at parity with the US dollar. Mandatory ITBMS registration is triggered when the taxable person's gross annual transfers exceed B/.36,000 or when the person habitually conducts business activities, imports goods, or renders specified taxable services regardless of amount.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama operates a mandatory electronic invoicing regime known as Facturación Electrónica en Línea, governed by DGI Resolution No. 201-3572 de 2021 and subsequent ANIP implementing resolutions. Taxpayers with gross annual income exceeding USD 300,000 are required to issue fiscal e-invoices through ANIP-authorised electronic billing operators, with real-time or near-real-time digital validation by the Sede Electrónica, unique invoice serialisation, mandatory digital signature and QR code, and an electronic packing/transmission requirement (FEC format) before consular or customs clearance. Export invoices must reference the corresponding customs export declaration in the SICEA/VUPE platform and maintain a zero-rate digital file for audit purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods physically leaving Panamanian territory qualify for the 0% ITBMS rate, provided that: (i) the exporter holds a valid RUC and customs exporter code; (ii) the goods are sold to a non-resident foreign transferee for use or consumption outside Panama; (iii) the transfer is a genuine export transaction supported by a lawful customs export declaration filed through SICEA; (iv) the invoice is issued in the exporter's name in US dollars or foreign currency; (v) payment is received via Swift LC or TT wire transfer from the foreign buyer into a Panamanian bank account; and (vi) export proceeds are settled and repatriated within the maximum 180-day window from the date of bill of lading. For a manufacturer of digital X-ray flat panel detectors under ISIC 3250 (vapor-deposited amorphous silicon caesium iodide DR detectors), eligibility further requires that the exporter verify the tariff classification under Panama's HS Chapter 90.22, maintain the underlying production cost records, and retain proof that the goods were neither consumed, modified, nor sold locally in Panama. Qualified exporters may claim refund or credit for ITBMS borne on production inputs (amorphous silicon, caesium iodide, glass substrate, electronics, cleanroom consumables) under the export refund mechanism, subject to ANIP documentary review.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Aduanas filed through SICEA/VUPE)
Bill of Lading (ocean or air waybill evidencing the goods left Panamanian territory)
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank confirmation of SWIFT LC or TT payment credited to a Panama bank account with B/. RFC reference)
Commercial Invoice (USD-denominated, referencing the foreign buyer's purchase order and HS 90.22 tariff code)
Export Manifest / Gate-Out Certificate from the bonded warehouse or production facility
Certificate of Origin (Panama, issued or validated by the competent authority, where preferential tariff claims apply)
Zero-rated ITBMS Export Schedule (digital annex to the monthly ITBMS return, listing each export invoice and its customs declaration)
Copy of the Foundation's RUC certificate and exporter registration record
Certified cargo photograph or container tracking record for high-value X-ray detector shipments
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ANIP conducts automated cross-matching between customs declarations (SICEA/VUPE) and ITBMS returns; any export invoice without a matching customs export declaration or without compliant FX remittance evidence is recharacterised as taxable domestic sales. The legal consequences of fraudulent or unsupported export zero-rating claims include: (i) immediate reversal of the 0% rate and reassessment of 7% ITBMS on the full gross value of the transaction from the shipment date; (ii) monthly surcharge of up to 3% and statutory interest for late payment; (iii) administrative fines ranging from one to two times the omitted tax; (iv) clawback of previously granted input VAT refunds, including retrospective recovery of export incentive benefits, plus harm (damages) of 100% of the refund; (v) for false customs declarations, criminal liability under Ley de Aduanas and the Código Penal for customs fraud, with potential imprisonment terms for directors and the fiscal representative; and (vi) suspension of electronic invoicing privileges and revocation of the exporter registration. Both the foundation and the responsible council members, registered agent, and fiscal representative may be jointly and severally liable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No formal central bank. The Republic of Panama uses the U.S. dollar as legal tender and maintains no domestic currency issuance authority. The banking and foreign-exchange supervisory authority is the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP), with Banco Nacional de Panamá acting as fiscal agent and the Ministry of Economy and Finance responsible for economic and financial policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Capital and current account transactions are fully convertible in U.S. dollars. Panama does not administer exchange controls, capital repatriation permits, or currency conversion quotas. A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) may receive foreign equity contributions, shareholder loans, trade proceeds, and client payments in USD and may remit dividends, loan repayments, supplier payments, and profit distributions to nonresidents without exchange-control authorization. The practical hurdles are exclusively compliance-driven: SBP-regulated banks require clear underlying transaction documentation, source-of-funds evidence, and ultimate beneficial ownership disclosure. Profit remittances by a nonresident PIF are generally free of Panamanian withholding if the underlying economic activity has no Panamanian situs; however, payments must correspond to documented trade, service, or financing transactions to avoid AML/CFT suspicion.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio in Panama. Exporters and trading entities may retain dollar receipts freely in domestic or offshore accounts. For AML/CFT integrity, banks expect export receipts to be reconciled against sales contracts, commercial invoices, customs declarations, transport documents, and shipping records. The absence of surrender rules does not waive bank due diligence or the obligation to identify the origin of funds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account for institutional and public-sector-linked clearing
Operational Account in USD with commercial letters of credit, SWIFT wire, and treasury management
Operational Account in USD with trade finance, commercial LC, and regional correspondent banking
Operational Account in USD with online banking, payroll, and business settlement services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM for payment initiation and LOW for regulated treasury custody. Offshore digital electronic money institutions (EMIs) are not recognized as Panamanian banks and cannot accept client deposits or provide local settlement accounts without being licensed or registered with the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá. A foreign EMI may be used as a payment gateway, card-issuing vehicle, or invoice-AP/AR tool, but all material clearing of medical X-ray flat-panel trade flows must settle through an SBP-licensed bank or its correspondent network. Treating an offshore EMI as a bank would create legal, AML, and counterparty risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the default expectation under SBP-aligned KYC practice. Most Tier-1 Panamanian banks require the foundation council members, protector, authorized signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners to attend an in-person interview at a bank branch, or to appear before a notary public in Panama for verification of identity and signature. Remote opening is permitted only in bank-specific risk-based programs for low-risk structures and generally requires apostilled corporate documents, notarized resolutions, electronic verification of identity, and a prior correspondent relationship. In practice, at least one director or authorized signatory must satisfy a physical or notarized in-person interview; fully remote video onboarding is rare and should not be assumed for a PIF holding an ISIC 3250 trading mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity of the Private Interest Foundation: the foundation council exercises broad discretionary powers and beneficiaries may not be publicly registered.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled Foundation Charter and Internal Regulations; current Foundation Council Resolution resolving to open the bank account and designate signatories; a sworn beneficial-ownership register declaring all beneficial owners above 10%; certified passports and tax identification numbers of each council member, protector, and UBO; current registered-agent certificate issued by a licensed Panamanian resident agent; express statement that no bearer shares or undocumented beneficiaries exist; and extract of the governing Panama Private Interest Foundation Law (Ley 25 de 1995).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear commercial substance of a Panama-only foundation trading digital X-ray flat-panel detectors (ISIC 3250) with suppliers and buyers in multiple jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OEM and distributor framework agreements; purchase orders, proforma invoices, commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, air waybills, and cargo insurance; product specifications and registration certificates for digital X-ray flat-panel detectors; ISO 13485/9001 or manufacturer quality certificates; end-user hospital or distributor letters of intent; regulatory import/export permits for medical devices; US FDA and EU CE certificates where applicable; transaction-flow diagram showing goods, shipping routes, payment flows, commissions, and final delivery destinations; and the foundation board-approved trade budget and business plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction profile inconsistent with foundation capital base: high-value pass-through payments or rapid turnover without a credible capital injection record.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder subscription agreement and bank-stamped proof of initial capital injection; audited or accountant-reviewed financial statements of the PIF; board-approved treasury policy and annual procurement plan; serialized invoice-level detail identifying each X-ray panel model, unit quantity, unit price, and shipment reference; external borrowing or loan agreements for trade-working-capital; tax compliance evidence, including annual Panama tax filings and receipt of municipal or fiscal payments; and historical bank statements showing predictable trade-cycle behavior aligned with documented contracts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections must be routed through the SWIFT MT103 interbank network into the foundation's USD operational account at an SBP-licensed Panamanian bank. The initiating shareholder or lender must execute the wire from the same legal entity or natural person named in the PIF ownership or loan documentation; third-party payers are generally rejected. The payment should contain the beneficiary foundation's exact legal name, account number, beneficiary bank BIC, and a payment narrative referencing the foundation charter and trade purpose, such as 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - PRIVATE INTEREST FOUNDATION - ISIC 3250 DIGITAL X-RAY FLAT-PANEL TRADE.' Panama does not maintain a government-assigned payment-purpose code framework, so the bank-validated SWIFT purpose narrative and underlying board resolution, subscription agreement, source-of-funds explanation, and sanctions/OFAC screening clearance form the compliance record. For trade prepayments, the narrative must cite the supplier invoice and contract number; for shareholder loans, cite the loan agreement and disbursement schedule.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary outbound clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for open-account telegraphic transfers to verified suppliers, freight forwarders, and service providers. For large or strategically critical shipments, the foundation should use an irrevocable commercial documentary letter of credit issued by a Panamanian bank via SWIFT MT700, payable against a clean-on-board bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, and quality or regulatory certificate. Confirmed or advised LC structures can reduce supply-chain payment risk for Chinese or regional manufacturers. Documentary collections using MT400/MT470 are permissible for lower-risk invoice-backed settlements. Domestic U.S.-dollar checks and local interbank debits are available through Panama's local clearing systems; cross-border USD clearing is executed through CHIPS or FEDWIRE via correspondent bank accounts. Every outbound disbursement must be supported by a signed contract, supplier invoice, and, where required, local tax or regulatory declarations; no cash disbursements should be made for trade settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/CNY deliverable FX forwards with an SBP-licensed bank, limited to the tenor and notional amount of documented supplier payments.
USD/CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for hedging CNY exposure while settlement occurs only in U.S. dollars.
USD/EUR and USD/KRW deliverable FX forwards for verified customer or supplier invoices in those currencies.
Cross-currency swaps between USD and CNY or EUR, permitted when the foundation demonstrates real trade exposure and maintains no speculative market position.
FX options and market orders are not recommended as a primary treasury instrument for a PIF unless separately authorized by the foundation council and supported by bank-approved risk policies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Tasa Única Anual de Persona Jurídica)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance, paid through the National e-Tax Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March of each calendar year, or within the month of the foundation's registration anniversary where the DGI anniversary-based payment calendar applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts a USD 300 surcharge plus monthly interest; continued default for 90 days triggers suspension of the foundation's certificate of good standing and legal capacity, and persistent non-payment may result in administrative strike-off by the Registro Público.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) via the electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March immediately following the calendar tax year; extended to 30 June when audited financial statements are attached and prior DGI authorization applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-filing penalty of 5% of the tax due, capped at 100%, plus statutory interest; serious or repeated non-filing permits DGI to assess presumptive income and revoke the foundation's fiscal good-standing status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Final Beneficial Owner and Transparency Confirmation (Registro de Transparencia y Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Beneficial Ownership Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March and within 30 calendar days after any change in foundation council membership or beneficial interest
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory fine of USD 500 per late declaration and up to USD 10,000 for material misrepresentation; unresolved non-compliance suspends issuance of the foundation's tax and good-standing certificates and may interrupt the resident agent's ability to act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Private Interest Foundation is not automatically required to undergo a statutory audit. An independent audit becomes compulsory only if the foundation carries on Panamanian-source commercial or professional activities with annual gross revenue above USD 1,000,000, is classified by DGI as a large taxpayer, or is expressly directed by DGI or the Registro Público. Non-commercial asset-holding foundations may maintain internal records without filing audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by the Accounting Board of Panama; cash-basis local GAAP is permissible only for tax-exempt, non-commercial foundations that are not subject to a mandatory audit.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The foundation must keep its final beneficial ownership information current with the DGI Transparency Registry. Any transfer of foundation interests or change in benefit entitlement must be confirmed in writing to the DGI within 30 days and reconfirmed annually by the resident agent as part of the March compliance cycle. Charter-level changes must also be notarized and recorded with the Registro Público; internal economic interest changes require only council minutes signed by the foundation council and resident agent.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 750 – USD 2,500 per year depending on the resident agent and service package
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Voluntary if not compulsory; market range USD 1,500 – USD 4,800 per engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% preferential statutory rate applicable to taxable income not exceeding PAB 1,500,000; territorial taxation exempts all foreign-source income; Private Interest Foundations deriving only foreign-source passive income are generally outside the scope of Panamanian corporate income tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 200 – Declaración Anual del Impuesto Sobre la Renta, filed through the DGI Oficina Virtual / e-Tax portal (https://ov.dgi.gob.pa).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year end; for calendar-year taxpayers, the return must be filed no later than March 31 of the following tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) – official tax identification number of the entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs must first obtain a RUC through a resident legal representative before filing; enter the nine-digit RUC exactly as registered.
Use the date consistent with the financial year applied in audited financial statements and bank records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Panama-source income from commercial, industrial and service activities carried out in Panama, including sales of digital X-ray flat panel detectors and related supplies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only income derived from Panamanian-source activities; foreign-source sales and passive investment income are exempt under the territorial system and must be excluded from this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source gross income for informational reconciliation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not compute tax on this amount; maintain supporting contracts, invoices and transfer pricing documentation to demonstrate the foreign source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized deductions attributable to Panama-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be directly allocable to Panamanian operations; any indirect expense attributable to exempt foreign-source income must be prorated and substantiated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income calculated as gross Panama-source income less authorized deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the result is a net loss, enter zero and carry it forward separately for the statutory five-year period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable statutory tax rate selection: 15% for taxable income up to PAB 1,500,000; 25% for taxable income exceeding PAB 1,500,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select the rate based on total taxable income after loss carryforwards and before tax credits; a non-resident PIF with no Panamanian-source taxable income enters zero.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross corporate income tax derived by applying the selected rate to the taxable income amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Computational field; ensure the rate applied matches the statutory thresholds and the filed supporting schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance income tax payments, monthly withholdings, and tax credits previously paid to the DGI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include certificates of withholding issued by Panamanian counterparties and bank transfer confirmations for advance payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or credit carried forward after applying payments and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any remaining tax must be settled electronically using the assigned reference code; overpayments may be credited to subsequent periods.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a monthly penalty of 3% of the tax due per month or fraction thereof, capped at 40% of the tax, plus annual late-payment interest of 1% per month. Failure to file within the statutory period after DGI notice may also result in automatic fiscal closure, administrative fines up to PAB 50,000, and cancellation of tax compliance certificates.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% general statutory dividend withholding tax; a 10% rate applies to distributions out of profits taxed at the preferential 15% bracket.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke tax treaty dividend relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit to the Panamanian withholding agent before the distribution: (i) a duly apostilled or legalized certificate of tax residence (TRC) issued by the home tax authority; (ii) Form 300 DTA declaration and ownership history; and (iii) an updated beneficial ownership declaration. The withholding agent must retain these documents and file the accompanying DGI schedule for DTA application. Relief operates prospectively and is not self-executing without prior documentary compliance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory withholding tax: 15% on royalties paid to non-residents for use of patents, trademarks or technical IP in Panama; 5% on interest paid to non-resident lenders on Panamanian-source loans. Treaty rates may be reduced to 5% or 0% on royalties and to 0% or 5% on interest depending on the particular DTA, provided the TRC and DTA relief protocol are satisfied.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File is triggered when annual related-party transactions exceed PAB 3,000,000; a Master File is required for multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue exceeding PAB 50,000,000. The Panamanian balboa (PAB) is pegged 1:1 to the USD.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), established under Law 70 of 2019, apply to entities conducting any 'relevant activity' such as distribution, intellectual property holding, financing or investment management. A Private Interest Foundation holding digital X-ray panel IP and earning royalties or intra-group distribution commissions must demonstrate adequate physical premises, full-time employees and strategic management in Panama. Passive asset-holding PIFs may rely on an licensed resident service provider, but must nevertheless file an annual ESR declaration. Inadequate substance may result in financial penalties, mandatory license revocation, automatic exchange of information and strike-off of the foundation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of Panama-source revenues, fabrication of deductible expenses, or using the PIF to conceal actual independent business operations conducted through a Panamanian branch.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction carries imprisonment of 5 to 10 years, a fine of up to PAB 1,000,000, re-assessment of omitted tax, surcharge of 50% of the omitted amount, and monthly interest of 1%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president, treasurer, legal representative and members of the foundation council who sign or cause the false filing are jointly and severally liable for civil restitution; courts may impose travel bans, assets embargo, disqualification from holding directorship in Panama, and, upon conviction, imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining all X-ray flat panel distribution and IP ownership in a PIF with no physical office, employees, or local board meetings in Panama while routing global sales through Panama to exploit the territorial exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties of PAB 10,000 to PAB 100,000 per fiscal year, mandatory removal of the foundation from the registry, invalidation of the tax residence certificate, inclusion in EU/CRS adverse listings, and exchange of information with foreign tax authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Founders, council members and the resident agent may be held jointly liable for unpaid penalties and assessed taxes; investigations may trigger precautionary travel bans and six-month administrative arrest while the assets are traced.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting sales prices below arm's length on intra-group invoicing of digital X-ray detectors, or paying excessive management royalties to the PIF without functional and risk analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI may re-determine taxable income using the most appropriate OECD method, apply adjustment of 25% of the understated income, plus a late payment penalty of 1% per month and fines of up to PAB 200,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved unrealistic intercompany price lists are personally liable if the PIF cannot satisfy the adjustment; they face civil restitution orders, asset freezes, and disqualification from acting as tax representatives.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain a beneficial ownership register, hiding the identity of the settlor or final beneficiary from the banking institution, or processing SWIFT wire transactions without complete AML/KYC documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 23 of 2015, fines of PAB 5,000 to PAB 500,000 per violation, suspension of the PIF's registration, and for money laundering activity criminal penalties of up to 15 years imprisonment and forfeiture of the proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Natural-person directors and the resident agent are personally liable for AML fines; they may be subject to travel bans, preventive arrest, civil forfeiture of personal assets, and long-term disqualification from operating regulated businesses in Panama.
